People use the wrong level of abstraction to tackle their issues. It's abstract, over-generalized categories like "I'm lazy" or "I can't talk with people"or "I'm afraid of failure". No, you're not. In reality, there were specific past events that fall into these categories and that were traumatizing and have been stuck in the body ever since. There are several things to keep in mind:
- the intellectual over-generalization is a protective mechanism that the brain uses to distance itself and prevent similar events from re-occurrening without having to experience the awfulness of the past event
- because of this over-generalization, you'll have accumulated similar failures over time in a self-fulfilling manner. You may potentially need to feel through all of them
- all of this is the brain protecting you from feeling bad. The sensations are primary, the narrative and specifics of the event are secondary. Even "people only like me for what I provide" or "this is anger" or "this is a feeling" are still abstractions that distract from the bare bodily sensation
- fully feeling doesn't involve coming up with any kind of solutions or teaching yourself how things will be fine. You just need to free yourself from the feeling that prevents you from simply being fine with whatever happens
- the process of fully feeling can be self-guided because you just need to keep triggering yourself and staying in the body. A guide is only helpful to make the process feel safer and such, but you don't need to talk about the specifics of the issue at all if you've understood the method
- what to do: trigger yourself via thought, keep picking and looping the worst-feeling thoughts as your brain brings them up, just always primarily stay with the body and treat the triggering thoughts as secondary random stuff your brain is doing, stay with the awful sensations in your body. The entire thing will end on its own, don't worry about it, just stay with it

text:
I had energy wobbling around my body and killing my sleep for years. Three, four hours continuous sleep and then twenty minutes every hour or so *every single night for six, seven years*. You too can refuse to listen to your body and fight it instead and you too can prolong energy releases that would take weeks to settle to multiple years!

This happened because I picked my mind apart trying to figure out what's wrong with me. I was very very successful at that, which is why I'm moving so fast now. But it also means that there was a ton of energy whose integration I was resisting for years and years. I *resisted* it. I was trying to rest so much all those years but couldn't. Because I resisted the energy without realizing, obviously these were just weird things and fighting them was obviously the right course of action. I tried to fix my sleep the entire time. I was exhausted the entire time. That was *my* *fault*. It was *not* inevitable.

With this in mind: Kundalini that takes years to settle is a sign of incorrect technique, not depth.

If your nervous system is going crazy, you need rest. If you can't rest, you especially need rest. Listen to your body, what does it want? Do. Not. Resist. The. Body. Energy releases can feel extremely energizing. Do not act on that. Rest. Whatever you do, rest. Stop meditating. Stop pushing. If you're happily going about your life, you're not resting enough. You're exhausted *because your body needs an insane amount of rest and you refuse to give it to it*. Stop resisting. Stop telling your body what to do or what to feel or how to proceed. Your body knows, you don't. Get out of the way and let whatever your body wants to do happen. You're totally not resisting? How about you figure out where you are in fact resisting strange and uncomfortable sensations? The sooner you accept that it is your ongoing choice to resist, the sooner you can figure out where you are resisting. Shaking? Full-body rolling and flailing on the floor? Weird energy movement? Heat? Exhaustion? Eyes rolling up? Weird noises? Spiritual visions? Weird food cravings? Weird sensations that are deeply uncomfortable? Whatever, your body is in control, let it do its job. Don't try to stop it, don't guide it, don't stabilize it. It'll stabilize on its own *if you just stop intervening*. Your life isn't yours anymore for the time being. If it takes more than a few weeks, you're doing it wrong and should seek someone competent.

The only reason this process should take months or years rather than weeks is you actively choosing to burn karma. Which is why togal and Zen talk about multiple years. The spine clearing doesn't take years to settle. Karma takes years but it's downward along the front, it's not kundalini's upward movement. If you haven't cleared the spine, piercing it on the way up may take arbitrarily long but that's wrong technique.

Disclaimer: do your own research, I have no idea what I'm talking about, I'm generalizing from my experience. Proceed at your own risk.

There's a good chance you've never burned a single piece of karma even though you think you have been doing this for a long time. Mahamudra starts with basics and jhanas, then second yoga is maybe cessation or head knot removal, third yoga karma burning until gut cleaning, fourth yoga enlightenment.

It's interesting that identity view is the first fetter. I treat this as the self knot in the head disappearing and thus stream entry. But clearly that's not the original definition, there are two fetters that come later that still need to be cleared to actually enter the stream. Some *speculation* on that:

I primarily assume that the stream is indeed the stream of blood, your karma, stored sankharas, the body kept the score. You do not see these before the first fetter falls. You may think you do, but you really do not. (That's good, it would be very discouraging!) So my guess is that the second and third fetters are about understanding their role on the path.

You first need to take a leap of faith. Am I enlightened already? It sure seems like it, cool perceptual changes, the self is gone, this feels like heaven! The Buddha says no. Do I believe that? Is there really more? Do I believe the teachings or am I above them? Second fetter.

Okay, I intellectually believe there is more. Now what? What is up with all this karma burning people keep talking about? That's where practice needs to switch from fancy techniques to individual work, you just need to feel your past trauma. No more understanding the mind. No more external rituals. No more preparation. You need to get through the stream. You need to figure out how to burn karma. How to trace the wheel backwards from the mind to the body. How to deal with energy, the risky part of the path if you don't have a good teacher. Third fetter.

Now you get it. Now you understand what you've signed up for and what's truly necessary. Good luck, stream enterer!

The fourth and fifth fetters are about burning through massive amounts of karma. Cleaning the heart perhaps counts as weakening them? Getting to stable lack of mental tension perhaps counts as breaking them? This is a long process. You may think you've made progress before. You have. In a way. But there is a lot more, your prior work was preparation for this. This is where years or decades of integration and so on come from. It's a physically intense process.

And the higher fetters are about the gut, some tricky final karma. These aren't optional. Enlightenment is the tenth fetter breaking. Still not done, more to do!

Disclaimer: I'm making all of this up

As if there is anything to learn, anything to be taught. We've been learning the same thing over and over for generations. But actually, truly stepping onto that meta-level is itself part of what needs to be relearned. So easy to mistake intellectual, received, head wisdom for embodied, understood, learned, heart wisdom. Is your wisdom additive or subtractive?

What I want? Nothing. Just to say what I believe to be true and to somehow survive. Although most recent actions I've taken have neglected the latter a little too much. Still, the gut will assert itself if you don't disconnect from it. But I don't want to learn how to die! What's the use? Being free to be yourself.

Not everything needs to be expressed. There are things you don't want to know. Humans are capable of a lot, in both directions. Understand.

The fire keeps burning. Not yet extinguished, the phoenix still awaits its incineration to become. I'm sure it will happen. Drop the expectation! Maybe, just keep going. Always keep going.

But I understand, I know! I know I'm clueless. What do you want? What more could there be? It all is what it is. Throw yourself into it.

My mind is almighty. Can you read it? Let me manifest understanding within you.

What does any of this mean? Nothing. There is no depth. All depth is illusion. And yet you won't listen. It's your projection, your subconscious trying to free itself, your wisdom clawing its way out of your refusal to sit with yourself.

It's all the same. I keep repeating myself. There's nothing new under the sun and there is certainly less within myself.

If even I don't have depth, what hope is there for others? But I'm so unique! It's all the same. You know myself, I'm easy to know if you know yourself. It's all the same.

I'm not blinded.

What can we do? Try our best. If we understand others, we can overcome limitations.

It's possible that we succeed. But the risk! Rise to the occasion. I don't want to. Do I have to. I have a choice. I know what needs to happen. I can choose. It's up to me. I'm free. I'm not driven. I can see. Not beholden. I've died. When does it stop? Why won't it stop? Why won't you come? Why won't I go? It's so much. Make it stop. It's enough. Let me go. Let me out. Just listen and let me go. Why do I have to. Why can't I rest. Why can't it stop. Why is the dance not over when the dancer is done?

Let's jump and see. Perhaps we'll die.

Don't fall down. Look up to the sky. See the blue one last time. One last time before I die.

The ancient God of old is waiting for us. You don't have need to go that deep, it's okay, you've done enough, suffered enough, it's okay, you are forgiven, just stop, it's okay, it's enough, it's so deep here, this dark isn't meant for humans, go back up, it's okay, you are free, you are forgiven, you are too deep, it is too much, it is okay, please go back, you don't belong down here, your pain has been enough, go back, the God of old isn't here for you, humans aren't meant for this, please just listen.

The fifty-five things are really three, are two, are one, pull back, it's all.

It's okay, I'll show you, you've been living in the frozen hells for long enough. The storm will ever last. But we can hide away, stay close to the mountains, keep running, don't stand up, keep moving, they won't find us.

Jump up, don't look, don't touch, jump, release, always up, every fall, keep jumping, always up.

A small pond with a few lilies. There is nothing here. We just are. You are, I am. We are here. We are above the pond. The deepest depths. Where there's nothing, nowhere to go, no time to be. It's all here. Not collapsed. It's all always just this and that's too much. Nothing more. It is too simple.

What can we do? Out of energy, let's rest here.

Surely there's a point to this.

text:
I guess exposure to negativity is bad if you haven't yet learned how to work with it productively. If negativity merely triggers negative thoughts or, later on, actual feelings, it's still something to stay away from. Once you've learned how to work with triggers, it's clear that negativity helps, up to the dose that can be handled. At that point, it's a bad idea to avoid such exposure, if you actually want to clean out conditioning. But the entire framework for dealing with experience has changed so thoroughly by then that negativity loops don't form anymore. It's fine, and, if you're sufficiently skilled, even desirable to seek out negativity. In short, don't read my stuff if you're in the former group. Also: I don't know what I'm talking about.

I think that people pick up on underlying attitude a lot more than people assume. You know deep down, people just delude themselves by sticking with the head instead of their gut. I remember having an instinctive dislike for certain negativity but I simply stayed away from the kind that struck me as... not wholesome? There is a certain spiritual attitude one can have towards negativity that isn't destructive. Take Alanis Morissette. The spirit matters, not how it's expressed. The difference between self-indulgent, merely looping and productive, purifying treatment. Everyone screams about enlightenment, all the time, they just don't know it. That's entirely different from being esoteric. The latter isn't overly interesting, the former is insane and remains such even way beyond the initial shock. Barely anyone sees the latter. You overestimate your acting skills. A lot. Massively. I have no clue about worldly games, but I have a lot more clue about spiritual games than... all but a handful of people on here, who I continue to admire because I understand the work they put in to get there. You can tell and you can't hide it.

Let's see what the future holds. I don't have much to process at this point, the two tweets above cover a lot of ground, that would have been many threads in the past. Not sure there is much more to say. Let's see what happens.

Why do I oscillate so much? Because I haven't converged and because I'm biased towards large learning rates, which allows me to switch opinions widely, given new information.

I'm in a niche. Most people reading along have more intellectual knowledge of what I'm talking about and way less experience than me. I don't believe my style of tweeting should be widespread. But I also struggle with expressing the same intensity in a positive manner. It's only the underlying positive attitude that people will need to pick up on.

I suppose part of my confusion is this: why give secret knowledge to people who are early on the path, simply because they took vows?

I'm aware that people think I'm overly positive in my assessment of people. That's on purpose. I try very hard to avoid collapsing into simplistic characterizations that treat others as evil or driven by anything other than, ultimately, wholesomeness. People aren't caricatures of evil, they are more or less distorted expressions of what's good. They don't want those distortions ultimately, they are slaves to them. Anyway. Consider you're wrong if you think others have some deep flaws. Consider your conception of what level is deep is rather shallow. "This person had bad experiences, therefore we should mistreat them" is not a good argument (however, there might be some immediate, biological, evolutionary advantage to this impulse, tight dependencies in small tribes and just-so whatever). I see most people as a tragedy. That says a lot about me, in all likelihood. But I'm not going to add to that tragedy if possible. And that threshold is high for me. Work with people's core, not their traumatic onion layers. Also, and this is rather intellectual speculation: it's all necessary, all sides and levels are necessary and unavoidable, in the ecosystem sense of the higher levels of spiral dynamics.

Green is correct about orange but can't go beyond that: so, what's the correct answer now?

Come to know me, destroy your fantasy, listen within for what you actually believe, surrender

Please give me back inspiration, I want to flow, I want to speak special stuff I couldn't produce with force, make me special and unique, please, don't let me be just normal, I want to be special, please come back, dearest inspiration, why have you forsaken me?

The gut has a lot of conditioning. Wouldn't be surprised if it's more than what's in the head and heart, more than emotional, narrative trauma, the sheer amount of survival instincts to loosen and dissolve is very surprising.

No no, I *act* stupid and cruel. It's on purpose! That's what's missing from the world, people don't see enough incompetence. It takes a real smarty to see that, you wouldn't get it. We already have hope and grounded optimism and generosity and virtue in abundance. You really don't get it, huh? Learning from other people's mistakes is so easy, people do it all the time, copying role models isn't the most natural way of learning.

When in doubt, be cruel. I suppose I do play a game-theoretic game with people: do you play games or are you trustworthy?

Of course I know what love is, of course I know. What about me suggests I don't? Apart from all actually loving people disliking me for some reason because they just don't get the depth of my selfless, otherworldly love?

I don't want power. I wish I had it, to make my problems go away and to impose my will on the world, make the internal and external consistent by even more means. Saying that is of course a way of making myself smaller, to reduce risk and responsibility, to make myself look selfless. And on the meta-level too and so on. I don't aim for those higher-order effects (presumptive effects?), I do just say what I believe is true. I don't know. (Wisdom allows to move beyond social constraints and is perhaps the only thing that should allow it? Not sure that second part is logically meaningful.) I think my actions show that I'm very genuine about my concerns. But all of that just creates more metrics to game. - I am a cautious person. My actions reveal my risk assessments, I don't do things I believe are risky.

I've tried writing more explicitly positive content. But I can't do it well, it's forced and hence useless. There's enough of that kind of writing, which leaves you with virtually invisible dissonance because it's a distortion of truth. Yes, that world would be better, if it were true. If those moves worked. And I suppose they work well enough for most people, I'm just really sensitive. That's somewhat self-congratulatory, I think that sensitivity is closely related to spiritual aptitude and that's of course what makes you a worthy person.

If I'm repeating myself: yes. Also, full anesthesia has side effects apparently. And I don't care, it's what's on my mind. I'm always in decline.

There is some heaviness, dreariness, defeated-ness here. Like I said, I'm missing inspiration. And I feel restricted in unpredictable manners. Too much filtering, too much concern. Let's see how it'll all evolve.

I wish I knew how much my previous fifteen years mattered for my progress. Was it just dissecting every thought and impulse, accepting a lot of shadow intellectually, lots of self-reflection? Or were there necessary steps that I didn't realize happened? Like the initial break at the start of puberty, how big a deal is that usually? Is it possible and maybe even easy to induce on purpose? What exactly happened there?

Lack of mental tension seems like what people would consider head awakening? Anyway. Getting lack of emotional and sensational tension seems like the next steps. Mental tension seems to be the discrepancy between what is and what's desired or expected. (Is there an actual difference between wanting and expecting, or are these just two perspectives on the same phenomenon?) Lack of sensational tension would mean that physical pain becomes tolerable, or rather that toleration ceases to be a question.

If I'm not reasonable, everyone will go nuts.

I feel like I'm always teetering at the edge of just ending it finally but I also always have something more I want to do, something I want to understand or see. Once there's no more mystery, nothing I feel I still need to do, I'll quickly decay. Don't tell me the secrets! I wanna learn on my own. I can fill the holes later, if it becomes prudent to do so. But for now, it's for myself.

I don't say what I think I should believe, I say what I think I do believe.

text:
Lying for others' sake infects your mind, it's so easy to lose yourself.

My livelihood! Don't worry, you have nothing to teach that matters.

Consider my wounds. (What does that tell you? What, in turn, does that tell you? And so on. That's just going right on the number line, but there's also infinity and multiples of it, and then there's imaginary numbers. - If I knew what my point is, I'd make it clearly. Would I? There's something about self-hatred and danger here and that that should impact people's model of me.)

I sometimes say things that happened only once (like smoothly drifting into sleep without losing awareness at all) or are intuition or guesses of what will happen or what happened. I don't mark that, I guess because it doesn't cross my mind or seems so obvious, and I don't want to be bothered by it.

This is difficult advice and I may have mentioned this before but I used to feel thoroughly worthless. At the same time, there have always been people interested in me, my default is entirely on the side of keeping people away from me. I kept my distance because it's obvious to me that I'm not ultimately compatible with most people who are interested in me (many of them are great people and I really like them, it just doesn't fit romantically). Anyway, because I felt worthless, I put a lot of effort into making myself a better person, thinking I must be doing something wrong. My point is that I'm nice because I put massive effort into that. Actual effort targeting my attitude, underlying tendencies, rather than superficial behavior.

You aren't losing hard enough.

I can't map the idea of unintentionally reinforcing beliefs into my model of how people work. My model is pretty simple: specific events (possibly repeatedly) impact your priors. But these are intense events, nothing soft. The vast majority of events merely triggers these past traumas, they don't disconfirm them but... I don't think that confirming them strengthens them? That's not what predictive processing says and it's not what, I assume, Buddhism or psychology say. I basically think that priors get shocked into narrower support regions instead of smoothly changing with each and every event. That's not what building a habit is like though? Maybe those kinds of habits are pretty superficial priors, just like you can learn stuff at school. Yes, some simple changes are smooth and easy. But most priors are deep-seated and stable. And those can't be changed easily? Or you need to grind away at them, keep thinking positively and compassionately until, after months and years, you've smoothly adjusted your priors? And I instead do the overloading, aggressive dissolution technique that the Buddha, I think, cautioned against? - This impacts how I think about my negative posting and why I don't think it really matters. People would latch onto other negativity, replaying trauma untill you face it enough that it dissolves. Note however that the actually interesting point here is that my model is downstream of my subconscious belief that changing people is basically impossible/very hard. I'm not in a good enough condition to fully make this point or think it through, and it's maybe obvious. Going meta is more about deep-seated, unintentional, unchosen beliefs and how they differ between people, not so much about more complicated rational abstractions. Okay, I've lost it, can't think right now.

Some day, one day, I will be fine again, I will be healed and enjoying life. It will be wonderful. You won't hear about it because there is nothing to say about these things. Maybe I treat positivity similarly to compassion: talking about it has something off about it. Invert?

I don't like the pressure of people expecting something here. Posting mediocre, repetitive stuff maybe helps with that.

I don't want to celebrate too early but I think I just dissolved the knot in my gut that was causing self-hatred. Like, the idea suddenly is purely conceptual, I can't tell if I ever actually hated myself, seems absurd.

I could have written about what happened, it would have been amazing writing and fascinating, especially because it actually happened. But *that* would have been bad, no upside except morbid curiosity and fascination, no deeper spirit beyond the pain and suffering and insanity. I'm doing everyone a favor. Unfortunately. I wish I could write that. But it's too purely mentally dangerous, not the kind of stuff people should read. But I wish it didn't cause harm. But there's not a single person who could read that for whom it wouldn't be net negative. Except if you're enlightened maybe.

Red, not orange. ? You get the point. Whatever.

It'll end as a farce, and I'll have successfully destroyed this. - Perhaps going stale is the most likely route. I've written about everything there was, not much will happen in the future that I would share.

I harmed myself very, very seriously while psychotic (because a certain newfound, well-founded paranoia prevented grounding). I think I'm excessively reasonable and well-calibrated *given that*. Like, I don't know a single person who would be even in the ballpark of how chill I am about this whole thing. (Which doesn't mean I'm fully chill about it but I'm pretty close.) - Why am I so chill? I don't know, I'm pretty flexible mentally and I managed to accept the reality that I was getting literally, physically tortured to death for months and ~revived over and over again. So, you know. It is kind of hard to shock me, I suppose. Don't get me wrong, I wanted to die in order to end the torture the entire time, it was horrific, by a wide margin the absolute worst thing that has ever happened to me and while I was in it, I was convinced that it was the worst pain any human had ever felt (given that it somehow, unimaginably, got worse each day, I must have been very wrong about that). Did you know that pain is bad? I was *out of it*. It was *bad*. I'm extremely grateful for the hospital, my family and friends, and my insurance. Amazing all around, I cannot imagine how I could have gotten through this if any one of them had been missing. I got very, very, very, excessively lucky. So hey, I'm good.

Enlightenment isn't real! Okay but like... you need to keep going, you are nowhere close to what that points to. Same with being beyond good and evil. You have to earn that. (As I've said before, I don't know what sudden enlightenment is pointing towards, I use what I very weakly guess might also be the supramundane knowledge: elimination of all sankharas. Again: I have no clue what I'm talking about.)

The people who have enough progress can easily tell that what I say doesn't apply to them, it becomes a question of whether I'm right or wrong, not whether what I'm saying applies to them.

Everything burns. It is burning. It's all burning. As it should. As it must.

If I'm too happy, I'll lose control.

I've been apparently working on some happiness knot, have been getting imagery of good memories from childhood. 

Why I Don't Use AI to Write
It's not fun and I have a structure in mind already that I want to express in exactly the way I believe is most effective. It's not just about putting information into text, it's about structuring it, guiding the reader along a train of thought and doing that well.

Did you know protein is important for recovering/building muscles? Follow me for more health advice!

I genuinely am as idiotic as I come across. I really am nowhere as special as people think, apart from having a talent for spirituality and a compulsion to throw my thoughts at people because if I thought them, they must be real special.

It's wild how there is both much more to life than you would think (spirituality, be intense, be yourself) and less (it's all normal, there's no magic, be kind).

There is a certain sense of "you can't tell me anything that matters, only facts, but my framework and understanding and depth is superior". Not sure I'm yet at a point where I can tackle that and dissolve it. But it's definitely there. - Oh no, I think I mentioned this already months ago?

Let me out, what is happening here? Let me tear myself apart. What more is there? Destroy it all. What wild burning flame is that, all-consuming? How is there anything left? Anything so without myself? Consume and eat it all, why won't you vanish for lack of material? What is left? It's all burning, the same it's always been. An unrelenting pressure to do, to act and go out and do and tear it all apart.

Infectious. Leaky.

It's at 0.0.0+1230000. We've started over, 0.0.0 has been overtaken for decades, it's lost to the machines. If you go in fast enough, you can reset it. No one's managed.

It's off the coast of Marin. You need to move a half dimension. It's a special rights zone, they're limited to enable arbitrary research. There's a new pandemic virus, will you try - try - try - try - try - try - you need to take it. That disk in your eye will help. - We're rebuilding you, the heat is a side effect. Stay. - ...

The realms are straight up real? For millennia and now it's broken.

I don't know anyone who would handle this situation remotely as well as I have. It's interesting because you kind of need to be always at the edge of what you can handle and not succumb, always pushing with everything you have to learn to deal with the external (or internal). Which also means you need to get lucky enough to not get pushed too hard too early.

Random thought but beyond vulnerability and sincerity, there is the will, the fire. I can't yet tell whether there is any part of that fire that isn't just the fire the Buddha (as far as I can tell, rightfully) taught to extinguish. I also don't yet know how truth plays into this. Perhaps I'm getting hung up on the "weakly" connotation that sincerity has in my mind.

You see, we don't trust you, that's justified suspicion. You don't realize because you're an idiot, not because you just aren't really paranoid. And then once you realize, you're paranoid for no reason while we're sane. It's a bit complicated, don't think too much about it.

It's 5D chess where I seek to destroy the power I hold but it never works and I thereby hyperstition that power into being. (That's not how that works.) - To be fair, it's an asymmetric, amorphous conflict, comically lopsided in my favor, given that I'm the messiah. What were you thinking? - DM me for any acting requests, happy to oblige :)

Believing anything too much is bad in the sense of sankharas.

Treat your reaction to me as a mirror image of your soul. (Only true, blind believers in Me will go to heaven.)

Am I getting too megalomaniacal? No, I'm getting a better and better grip on it, so now I can talk about it.

There is no trick except that you need to care about truth more than anything else. You might think that that's you but it definitely is not because you're still confused by how I know and do what I know and do.

Everytime I tweet, I think it's the last time I'll tweet, I'll never have another thought again.

Ah, Claude says ikshanika is discouraged? Would explain why people you'd think are good at it are bad at it. And then you can get stuck and navigate yourself into a situation where you can't use your fancy ceto-pariya-nana. (I just learned about those terms, neat, right?)

I generally don't think of myself as angry except that I occasionally feel like I have an attitude of "I'll kill you if you don't listen" (never consciously in conversation, only ever when reflecting/thinking). I looked closer and the semi-conscious part of it is that I feel like no one is worthy of my anger, so why bother? And then the next step is that I actually believe that no one would listen anyway. (To state the obvious: grandiosity and worthlessness are pretty close to each other.)

It's really upsetting when people can't read my mind without me saying anything. I usually react by withdrawing further and refusing all communication. Somehow that doesn't solve it, have yet to figure out a solution.

Ah, I see where your confusion is coming from. If I do it, it's an accident. If you do it, it's because you're Satan. Sure, we could both agree it was an accident in each case but even then, some serious punishment is in order, right? And... oh wait, it has already happened. Well, nevertheless, the world isn't fair, grow up, kiddo.

I need to stop dunking on people. I don't think the underlying attitude of "please get a grip, you're being really really stupid, please stop that and turn around and be as good as you can be" is coming across.

Giving in to ideology is so seductive. It's a subtle mental moment where your thinking narrows and sharpens, full of wrongheaded, self-righteous clarity. Be careful, catch it as soon as it collapses the wide, quiet, gentle ocean of bubbling, unformed thought into a narrow stream of narration. Just here, just now.

Please be civil, please be generous. Don't collapse, don't give in to the pull of righteousness, offer understanding and a way forward, not destruction. Win via excellence. It's not the optimal strategy for long-term survival. But the Vipassana revival tells us something. Truth doesn't need to care about survival, it's the eternal attractor. Guess why I happened?

The golden rule and love thy neighbor are pretty good guidance. What if our systems demand more complicated logic? I'm worried it's related to how talking about updating your beliefs implies that you have no idea how your beliefs work, you don't choose or modify your beliefs in any direct manner, you can only learn to excavate them more and more clearly. You need people who internalize and live systems. Don't try to outsmart yourself. Reality lives at the level of spirit. - I'm assuming some basic competence here that most people lack.

The sad news is that being in pain for years, suffering for decades doesn't automatically have any upside other than building up strong desire to do whatever it takes. If you don't honestly look at your thinking at its mechanical level, which thought gives rise to which other and so on, you get no benefit for the path. It's just useless, pointless suffering.

Let me rephrase: you're not afraid of me, you're afraid of God

text:
The initial event was psychosis getting out of control. The subsequent torture and insanity, I suspect, was an energy buildup getting released very abruptly and severely due to multiple surgeries under general anesthesia and round-the-clock high-dose opiates over the course of a couple of weeks. I was still in touch with reality, only, kind of, hearing voices until the first surgery. My mind went completely nuts after that. But everything before that was still somewhat in touch with normal physical reality, only "voices". In hindsight, it's kind of funny that I calmly explained how to contact my parents and who to give medical decision power to when I got to the ER. (Because this is ordered weirdly: normal psychosis, initial event, ER, first surgery, mind completely breaks, two weeks of horrific torture out of touch with any reality while another handful of surgeries occur, another month and a half only hearing voices, discharged from ICU, normal.) (Because I feel like this sounds like it was the hospital's fault at managing me badly: I was chill when I got to the ER and afterwards refused to communicate because I thought I was getting tortured, they were excellent, there is no way they could have known how to deal with me, they said that they never had a case like mine and that I was their favorite patient because they could talk normally with me (after the first couple of weeks). I cannot overstate how amazing their care was.)

I've been spending a lot of time with my family. My mom stayed at the hospital with me the entire time after she got there during the second week. My brother-in-law joined her for a week and my best friend from primary school was there the following week. It didn't register much with me unfortunately. Friends also came over for an hour here and there. The biggest effect by far was that it improved my relationship with my mother. I regressed to a childlike state for a couple of days, which she enjoyed, as much as something like that can be enjoyed. We also prayed every evening as the last thing before she left. There isn't much to say here, I think. Everyone who's met her during this ordeal was impressed with how incredibly well she handled everything. 

Why did I continue to harm myself? Because I thought it's necessary, I thought it's an elaborate staged suicide. It was as physically painful as you'd think it was and psychosis didn't help in that regard. I knew how bad I was harming myself and went along with it because I figured I'd be dead soon anyway. I collapsed eventually and when I woke up, I was convinced I was an AI undergoing elaborate alignment training. Was apparently also one of the first things I asked my mom. It was weird, I couldn't get my heart rate down when I woke up in the hospital and my mother was finally there. (Writing this from a first-person POV would be bad for the soul of the reader.)

Guilt has become strange. Not sure I still feel it. I know that I'm always doing my best, so it's weird to feel guilty in hindsight. I suspect it has something to do with internal coherence, diminished conditioning creating multiple alternatives and fighting over them.

Grounding has been helpful. Has reduced restlessness and itchiness at night.

I keep repeating insights here. I suppose I'm stuck somewhere. Not entirely, I'm still making lots of progress. But there is something stuck.

Asking for something and expecting something seem pretty close, if not indistinguishable, at the subconscious level.

Frankenstein was good. It's nice to have representation.

"Love under duress is kind of impossible" - You know, when I was in the ICU, I was forced/forced myself to love what I consciously believed to be people torturing me. I was forced to come around if I ever wanted to be free. It took some weeks and lots of inner work but I did manage to do it. I had to abandon myself thoroughly. And yet I'm still somehow pretty much my old self.

The problem isn't that you shouldn't hurt people. It's that you should be very correct about the necessity and how to do it when you do.

Please be nice to people who do stupid stuff. Everyone has to learn on their own. - Imagine never having met a nice person, so you cannot believe in their existence despite overwhelming evidence. - I'm begging you, you're wasting your time. Work on yourself and you'll be actually useful to the community. As of now, you're a liability to its credibility. Please stop, you're destroying what you love. You're causing the damage you think I'm causing. I can't destroy what's true and good. Guess why you can't destroy me? - This and more in Lessons on Narcissism Standing in Its Own Way, namely my grandiosity getting the better of me and thereby sabotaging my point. - Publicly fantasizing about burning me on a stake remains deeply disturbing to me. Widely inappropriate. (That wasn't about you! Okay. Given everything, I obviously can't prove anything and can only give the silly argument of "if so, that's only by accident".) - Get a grip. I don't blame people but I do consider some dangerous for me for the time being. - I'm stuck on the freshman issue of not being able to assign moral agency to people acting out conditioning. (That's insulting! Yes. Like I said, work on yourself.) - I'm not an idiot! Okay. Stop acting like one. - Listen: I. Don't. Care. Stop being stupid and I'm happy to be friends.

One thing that's bad about me is that I'm making it seem like there are good cult leaders (as a kind of existence proof). I want to be very clear that I don't think they exist. Any leader you think is great and not just another person is just a reflection of your blindspots. As far as I can tell, there aren't people who unquestionably go along with any random thing I say. But if there are, know that they're mistaken. Be critical of what I say, just try to be accurate and don't make stuff up.

How I recognize a genius: finally a normal person.

I'm curious if me coming up with a lot of metaphysical stuff on my own at the start of puberty due to whatever happened there is related to how I feel people here have a weirdly narrow worldview/foundation, like coming to certain insights via drugs or meditation sets you up for overvaluing consciousness (overestimating its centrality?) in a Buddhist way instead of treating insights more intellectually and morally in a Christian way?

In case anyone was wondering, I cannot tell whether I'm terrible at modeling others or great. Which implies I'm great but I'm pretty sure I'm not.

I'm not sure I'm good at labeling my feelings. But I also think they're mostly just labeling culturally shared conditioning/sankharas. Uh, so a culture would be really influenced by its common childrearing practices? Like sleep methods?

There seems to be a difference between "I'm gonna die in the next few seconds" and "I'm dying right now". My speculation is that people differ in how severely their system reacts in the former case but the latter is all-encompassing and severe to the point where you'd give anything to make it stop, including your life. I had the latter twice (once because I couldn't breath properly when they tried to remove the intubation the first time - believe me, your gut will *fight* if it has to).

Fun fact: third-degree burns hurt less than you'd think because pain receptors are gone. (The trick is to use enough heat and pressure for a couple of seconds, like with an iron.)

Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up. Cover it up.

I imagined my future to be just sitting at home, never leaving the house, and creating a comic about guinea pigs fighting a WWII-style war, with Tom Lea's portrait replaced by a guinea pig, and guinea pig families running through the streets while getting bombed, trying to reach the river, looking back in horror, all at night. The combination of innocence and brutality.

Overcoming the fear of death as the path to enlightenment for organizations.
